title: Community group calls for charges against off-duty Chicago officer after Little Village shooting
text:
Residents and activists in Chicago's Little Village neighborhood are calling for criminal charges against an off-duty Chicago police officer after a shooting that injured two men and a block riddled with bullets.
A community group is calling for charges to be filed against an off-duty Chicago police officer after a Little Village shooting at 24th and Rockwell.
Residents and activists in Chicago's Little Village neighborhood are calling for criminal charges against an off-duty Chicago police officer after Signs of the shooting remained visible Tuesday along 24th Street between Washtenaw and Rockwell avenues, where a vehicle and a nearby home were struck by bullets. According to the Civilian Office of Police Accountability, the shooting began early Oct. 4 after an exchange of words between the off-duty officer and a person in a group gathered on the block.
COPA said the officer fired multiple shots, then drove east toward South Rockwell, exited the vehicle and fired additional shots from two firearms simultaneously in the direction of the earlier encounter. One person was struck by gunfire, and another sustained injuries related to the incident, according to COPA. The agency said third-party video captured both shootings.
The Chicago Police Department said a man from the group physically engaged with the officer and struck him in the face before the first shots were fired. That allegation was not included inMLB Postseason 2026: Chicago White Sox hosting Cleveland Guardians, lead ALDS series 2-1 | LIVE UpdatesMembers of the Little Village Community Council returned to the scene, Thursday, distributing flyers and demanding that the Cook County State's Attorney's Office pursue attempted murder charges against the officer and that the Chicago Police Department terminate him.
"We have an officer that is a rogue officer, an officer that doesn't follow procedures, who fails to understand that there are laws," said Baltazar Enriquez of the Little Village Community Council. The shooting remains under investigation by COPA. The officer has been placed on administrative leave in accordance with department policy.
